blindSummary:
This state/province was the fifth of five to adopt a regional "anti-LGBT ideology" resolution by June 2020, completing a configuration that at peak covered about a third of national territory across roughly 100 municipalities and five regions. It sits in the same conservative-voting band as two neighbouring state/provinces, and its resolution was annulled or repealed in the 2020-2021 wave of court rulings and pressure from a supranational body.

No march ban, violence episode, or holdout municipality comparable to the findings in those two neighbouring state/provinces is documented at the state/province scale. The visitor-facing signal is the regional declaration's intent to exclude LGBTQ public presence and the social climate of the conservative-voting belt; the formal legal document is now absent.

Local risk sits above the country-wide average, identical to one neighbouring state/province on shared evidence: both are resolution-carrying state/provinces within the conservative group, without unit-specific enforcement or violence findings beyond the declaration itself. It is safer than a neighbouring state/province that additionally contains the country's first-ever anti-LGBT municipal resolution (in a town of about 40,000).
